exposure: delay in recognising problem requiring transfer to hospital
cohort: The cohort consisted of 215 women with multiple Caesarean Sections (CS) delivering at Iringa Regional Referral Hospital.
finding: The prevalence of adverse maternal (31.6%) and foetal (24.2%) outcomes among women with multiple Caesarean Sections was high, with significant predictors including lack of third-trimester ultrasound, emergency CS, and delays in seeking care.
mod_finding: Emergency Caesarean Section was identified as a strong predictor of adverse maternal outcomes among women with multiple CS.
cross-section timing: At the time of delivery/hospital stay in the maternity ward.
